newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks slide on profit-taking, await Q2.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks slide on profit-taking, await Q2.

text.p: Mexican stocks ended down for the second session in a row on Monday after sliding for most of the session.
Dealers said investors took more profits after last week's post-election buying spree, but volumed thinned as the market awaited second quarter corporate earnings.
"The market is in a consolidation period and very much awaiting second quarter earnings," said Gerardo Copca, an analyst at the Finamex brokerage.
The blue chip IPC share index ended down 44.55 points, or 0.92 percent, at 4,777.07.
Trading volume was much reduced from last week's record-breaking sessions at 73.1 million shares.
"Profit-taking is very healthy after recent gains, the thin volume tells you we're just consolidating," Copca added.
Dealers, meanwhile, said they saw a small outflow of foreign investment on jitters triggered by a slide on Wall Street and a sharp drop in Brazil.
"Brazil and New York hit us. Volume was thin, but we saw foreigners step out," a desk trader said.
On Wall Street, the Dow Jones ended up just 1.16 points at 7,922.98, but had gone as low as 7,860.03.
In Sao Paulo, Brazil, the Bovespa index plunged 454 points to 12,699.
Dealers said profit-taking was most notable in Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) and financial company Bancomer.

Telmex clipped 20 centavos (2.5 cents) off its recent advance to end at 20.80 pesos ($2.65). The telecommunications company's American Depositary Receipts followed suit and ended down 9/16 at 53. Bancomer inched down 4 centavos (0.5 cent) to 4.15 pesos
Dealers said the few briskly traded prominent gainers were stragglers like food packaging company Grupo Herdez, which ended up 24 centavos (4 cents) at 5.14 pesos (65 cents).
On the broad market, sliders outpaced gainers by 57 to 38, out of 115 stocks that changed hands.
